title: The SMT-LIB Standard: Version 2.7
credit_lines: The SMT-LIB Standard, Version 2.7 (release 2026-09-09), by Clark Barrett, Pascal Fontaine and Cesare Tinelli, hosted verbatim with its copyright and permission notice (page 2). BSmtLib, its Lean formalisation of the lexicon, grammar and parser, by Jan Onderka, Armin Biere and Henrik Böving, at 42b45c2 (MIT OR Apache-2.0). The links from the standard's passages to the Lean, the plain titles and the comparisons were made with AI and have not been reviewed by the authors.
companion_credit: Paper and Lean by Clark Barrett, Pascal Fontaine and Cesare Tinelli, from their repository onderjan/blazing-smtlib at 42b45c2.
licence: Verbatim copies only; the copyright and permission notice is on page 2 of the PDF
host: Hosted by Will Cook in his reading library, with credit to the authors.
review: The links from the text to the Lean, the plain titles, the reading notes and the comparisons were made with AI and have not been reviewed by the authors. No mathematician has reviewed them.

source.lean_scope: Lean 4.34.1 compiled the BSmtLibSpec library of BSmtLib, by Jan Onderka, Armin Biere and Henrik Böving, unchanged at 42b45c2. The example proofs under BSmtLibSpec/Facts are shown as source.

topics.name: Source text and tokenization
topics.description: Source files are divided into lexical tokens, with whitespace and comments separating them.

topics.name: Character classes
topics.description: The lexical rules distinguish whitespace, printable characters, digits, and ASCII letters.

topics.name: Numeric literals
topics.description: Numerals, decimals, hexadecimal literals, and binary literals each have a prescribed spelling.

topics.name: String literals
topics.description: Double quotes delimit strings, and doubling an interior quote gives the language’s single lexical escape.

topics.name: Symbols and reserved words
topics.description: Symbols, keywords, and reserved words supply the names and fixed vocabulary of the language.

topics.name: S-expressions and constants
topics.description: Special constants and other atoms combine into possibly empty parenthesized S-expressions.

topics.name: Indexed identifiers
topics.description: Identifiers are symbols, optionally qualified by one or more numeral or symbol indices.

topics.name: Attribute syntax
topics.description: An attribute consists of a keyword with an optional special constant, symbol, or parenthesized list as its value.

topics.name: Sort expressions
topics.description: Sort expressions are identifiers, optionally applied to one or more sort expressions.

topics.name: Term grammar
topics.description: Terms combine constants, identifiers, applications, abstractions, quantifiers, local definitions, matches, and annotations.

topics.name: Variables and scope
topics.description: Local variable declarations associate names with terms or sorts and determine the scope of their occurrences.

topics.name: Pattern matching
topics.description: Flat constructor patterns, variable patterns, and wildcards describe the cases of a match expression.

topics.name: Term annotations
topics.description: Attributes attach additional information to a term without changing its logical meaning.

topics.name: Scripts and solver interaction
topics.description: Scripts sequence commands that control a solver and request its responses.

topics.name: Declarations and definitions
topics.description: Sort, datatype, constructor, selector, and function declarations describe the components introduced by commands.

topics.name: Command syntax and options
topics.description: Command productions specify their arguments, including option attributes and information flags.
